hypothesis: A prior explicit-shuffle warp-first candidate was valid and faster than the baseline in repeated full-program measurements, but those measurements do not prove the block-local tree is the bottleneck. This contrasting experiment replaces its warp shuffle stages with the SM80+ native integer warp reduction, retaining a shuffle fallback, to test whether warp-reduction instruction cost matters while keeping the 128-thread tile and recursive launch structure unchanged. Unsigned modulo-2^32 intermediates plus an in-range final conversion preserve correctness when the exact final sum fits int32.

The prior candidate passed all 10 supplied cases (n=1, 127, 1024, 65536, and 4194304, two seeds each), with guards intact and input unchanged. transformations: Replaced explicit warp-shuffle reduction with __reduce_add_sync for SM80+ and retained the shuffle fallback for lower architectures; applied this warp-first reduction both to input values and the cross-warp combine.

Used unsigned 32-bit modular arithmetic for all partial sums and an explicit in-range conversion when storing the resulting bit pattern as int, avoiding signed intermediate overflow when the final exact sum fits int32.

Retained the 128-thread tile, zero-filled tail handling, four warp partials, recursive host stages, scratch-bank offsets, ABI, and default-stream ordering; set output to zero asynchronously for n <= 0.
